$comment: Art packs installed by `npm run assets:fetch`. The game is fully playable with none of
them installed — every animal, prop and level surface has procedural geometry, and
AssetLibrary falls back silently when a file is missing. Installing a pack is a visual
upgrade, never a gameplay change: colliders, grips, hitboxes and every movement constant
come from level and player data, so a mesh swap cannot alter balance.
Every entry MUST declare a licence and, for anything that is not CC0, an author — the
fetch script refuses to install an entry that does not, and packs.test.ts asserts it.
`sha256` pins the exact bytes we vetted the licence of, so an upstream file being replaced
fails the build loudly instead of silently shipping something we have no licence for.
Packs behind a click-through (Quaternius, Kenney, Synty) cannot be fetched by URL. Declare
them with "source": "manual", download the archive by hand, and run:
The script then resolves each file out of the archives it finds there.

packs.title: Fox (glTF sample asset)
packs.author: PixelMannen; rigging & animation by tomkranis; glTF conversion by @AsoboStudio and @scurest
packs.note: Model is CC0-1.0; the rigging, animation and glTF conversion are CC-BY-4.0, so the pack as shipped requires attribution.

packs.title: Ultimate Animated Animals
packs.author: Quaternius
packs.note: 12+ rigged animals with walk/run/jump/idle cycles in glTF. CC0, so it can ship in a web build with no attribution obligation — credited anyway. Behind a click-through: download by hand, then `npm run assets:fetch -- --from <dir>`.

packs.title: Stylised Nature / Jungle kit
packs.author: Quaternius
packs.note: Trees, rocks and foliage for the decorative props layer only. LevelDef.props is a separate list from LevelDef.colliders precisely so decoration can never change where a surface can be climbed.
